lines.text: Most kids fit a triangle in a square like THIS.
lines.caption: Most kids fit a triangle in a square like THIS.

lines.text: But that's NOT the biggest one!
lines.caption: But that's NOT the biggest one!

lines.text: The square has side one, and all three triangle sides are equal.
lines.caption: The square has side one, and all three triangle sides are equal.

lines.text: What's the largest area it can have?
lines.caption: What's the largest area it can have?

lines.text: Here's the trick. Pin one corner, and turn the triangle.
lines.caption: Here's the trick. Pin one corner, and turn the triangle.

lines.text: Watch the side. It grows, then shrinks again.
lines.caption: Watch the side. It grows, then shrinks again.

lines.text: The biggest one sits at fifteen degrees, balanced on the diagonal.
lines.caption: The biggest one sits at fifteen degrees, balanced on the diagonal.

lines.text: Its area is two root three, minus three.
lines.caption: Its area is two root three, minus three.

lines.text: That's about forty-six percent of the square. Flat only gets forty-three!
lines.caption: That's about forty-six percent of the square. Flat only gets forty-three!

lines.text: Why exactly that? The full lesson shows two neat ways, plus every trap.
